info.title: Provision LLM Engine API
info.description:
OpenAI-compatible + native endpoints exposed by the Provision LLM Engine (llama-server). Served by the server itself, so "Try it out" runs same-origin (no CORS setup needed). In router mode, send a known model id in the `model` field (e.g. `qwen2.5-chat`, `gte-qwen2-embed`).

**Licensed builds** (image `:release`): endpoints tagged _counted_ are metered by the license subsystem. A request is charged one unit per result it produces (a `prompt` / `input` / `documents` array or `n` > 1 counts per element) and only when a 2xx result is delivered; errors and requests the client abandons are not charged. The trial allows 50 requests per install; after that, or with no / an expired license, counted endpoints return HTTP 403 with an `error.license` block and `X-License-Mode` / `X-License-Used` / `X-License-Limit` headers until the product is activated via `POST /license/activate`. Endpoints tagged _exempt_ (health, metadata, tokenize, models, slots, `/license/*`) never consume the budget. Unlicensed builds (`:dev`) have no counter and answer 404 on `/license/*`.

Many routes have aliases (legacy / non-`v1` forms); the canonical path is documented and its aliases are listed in the route description.

**Admin API** (`/admin/*`, tag _Admin_): present only when the server runs in router mode with `PROVISION_ADMIN=1` (otherwise these paths answer 404). In the Docker deployment, and with the host nginx site of `deploy/linux/`, the nginx front door forwards `/admin` (and `/cors-proxy`) only for allow-listed client addresses and answers 403 to everyone else. Every endpoint except the `GET /admin/status` probe also needs the admin key in the `X-Admin-Key` header (use **Authorize**). Loading, unloading, downloading and deleting downloaded models keep using the public model routes (`/models`, `/models/load`, `/models/unload`); the settings, the upload of GGUF files (`/admin/models/upload*`) and the deletion of models of the models directory (`/admin/models/delete`) are protected by the admin key. Changes made through `/admin`, refused admin requests, actions of the server itself and some effects of the public model routes are recorded in an activity log (`GET /admin/audit`). Admin endpoints never consume the license budget.

post.description:
Send any subset of the three settings; fields that are left out keep their value. The request is validated as a whole: on any error nothing is saved. On success the settings are stored in the admin state directory, applied immediately and returned.

- `models_max`: applies to every later scheduling decision. Raising it takes effect at once; lowering it does not unload anything by itself.
- `pinned`: a pinned model is never unloaded to make room for another one. At least one slot must stay free: `pinned` must be shorter than `models_max`.
- `default_device`: GPU for models that have no `device` of their own (downloaded or dropped-in models; sections of `models.ini` are not touched by it, they get a GPU of their own through `POST /admin/models/settings`). A name this server does not have is not applied (`warnings`: `default_device_not_present`). Changing it rebuilds the model list, which unloads a **running** model whose arguments changed. Rejected with 409 while `MODEL_DEVICES` contains a `*=` entry.

**Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Change one model's settings, optionally restart it (exempt)
post.description:
Sets custom settings of one model (a value) or removes them (`null`); keys that are not given stay as they are. `reset: true` removes all custom settings of the model (also for an entry in `unattached`). Only the whitelisted keys of `AdminModelSettingsInput` are accepted; `cache-type-k` and `cache-type-v` must be equal; a quantized KV cache needs flash attention other than `off`. A value equal to the built-in default with nothing inherited counts as "not set", so it never changes anything.

- Model **running** and the change needs a restart: refused with 409 `restart_required` unless `restart: true`; nothing is saved. With `restart: true` the model is stopped first (at most its stop timeout + 10 s, else 504 `stop_timeout` and nothing is saved), then the settings are saved, the model list is rebuilt (like a rescan: models that were loaded and are down afterwards are loaded again, `restarted_also` / `not_restarted`) and the model is started again.
- Model **not running**: saved; with `restart: true` also loaded right away ("Save and load").
- New settings are first tried (`phase` `trial`); after two failed starts in a row the server goes back to the last settings that worked (`reverted`).

The POST holds the request until the restart has begun (up to the stop timeout + 10 s); follow the load on `GET /models/sse`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Will these settings fit? Dry run by llama.cpp (exempt)
post.description: Runs a short helper process of the server binary with the arguments the model would get with these (unsaved) settings. It uses llama.cpp's own fit machinery: the model and its context are built without allocating the weights, and the need per GPU (model, context, compute) and on the host is reported. The verdict per GPU compares the need plus a 1 GiB margin with the memory `available` there (free now, from the vendor tool or the helper, plus the model's own use if it is running and would be restarted); `verdict` is the worst of them. A model that uses no GPU (a CPU-only server, or `device` `none`) gets the verdict `cpu_only`. One check at a time (409 `check_busy`; 409 `check_stuck` while a stopped helper has not exited), at most 30 s. A result is reused (`cached`) for at most 60 s, while the model's effective arguments, the GPU inventory and the model's state (running or not) are unchanged and the live free memory of its GPUs moved by less than 256 MiB: llama.cpp's fit adapts the values left on auto to the memory free at that moment. `checked_while_running` marks a dry run made while the model was running (its fit saw the model's own memory as used). Nothing is saved. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

get.description: Every GPU of the server with total / used / free memory and the models placed on it. GPUs come from the inventory the server takes at start-up (and on `POST /admin/gpus/rescan`) in a helper process: names, backend, PCI bus id, memory. Live memory comes from the vendor tool of each GPU vendor found (`nvidia-smi`, `amd-smi` or `rocm-smi`, see `PROVISION_ADMIN_GPU_PROBE`), matched to the GPUs by PCI bus id; without one the inventory values are shown with their age. The router itself creates no GPU context. In `auto` mode `amd-smi` / `rocm-smi` are also looked for in `$ROCM_PATH/bin` and `/opt/rocm/bin`. One vendor-tool run at a time, at most 15 s each; a request waits for it at most 5 s (then `timeout`; the late answer is used by the next request), and a tool still running after its 15 s is reported as `probe_stuck`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

get.summary: Uploads: availability, limits and the uploads of this server, or one upload (exempt)
get.description:
Without `id`: whether GGUF files can be uploaded on this server (`available`; else `reason`: `no_models_dir`, `models_dir_missing`, `not_writable`, `staging_unusable`, `staging_other_filesystem`, and `message`), the fixed `limits`, every upload of this server (from every browser and admin, finished ones for 24 h, so a client that lost its files can offer to continue), `staging_bytes`, and whether the placement of an upload can be saved (`settings_writable`).

With `?id=<upload id>`: one upload with everything a client needs to continue it. Per file: `offset` (the bytes the server accepted; the next chunk starts here), `durable_offset` (on disk at the last checkpoint; after a restart of the server `offset` goes back to it), `complete`, `dropped`, `role`, `sha256` (computed while the file is received), `head_crc32` (CRC-32 of the first MiB, to compare with a file picked again; null while the server does not know it: then probe with `verify=1` of the chunk route), `final_name`, `header` (the header check of that file: `state`, and once the metadata was read `arch` and `type` as `general.architecture` / `general.type` of the file, `split`, and a `message` only with a warning or a refusal) and `error` (why the file cannot be used). The upload: `state` `receiving`, `checking` (`substate` `queued`, `hashing` with `progress`, `classifying`, `load_check`), `ready` (`blocked_by` `manual`, `name_taken`, `publish_error`, `check_failed`, `sha256_mismatch`, `settings_not_saved`, `settings_invalid`; details in `blocked`), `publishing`, `published` (`result`), `rejected` (`error`), `cancelled`, `expired`; plus `checks` (one per file whose header check started; `message` empty while all is well), `plan` (the final layout), `facts` (what the checks read), `warnings`, `last_activity`, `expires_at` (72 h without progress, counted while the server runs; set while `receiving` or `ready`), `idle_ms` and `last_client_idle_ms`.

The upload routes never answer 404 for an upload (the server replaces the body of every 404); an unknown or removed upload is 410 `upload_gone`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Create the upload of one model, or check it (dry run) (exempt)
post.description:
One upload is one model: a single GGUF file, or a complete split set, plus at most one projector (`mmproj`). Draft models are not supported (400 `unsupported_file`, `reason` `draft`, `file`).

- `name` becomes the model id: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`; refused without regard to case: containing `mmproj` or `.gguf`, starting with `mtp-` / `dspark-` / `dflash-` / `eagle3-`, containing `-NNNNN-of-NNNNN`, ending in `.`, Windows reserved names (400 `invalid_name` with `reason`). It must be unique, without regard to case, among the ids and aliases of the model list, the entries of the models directory as the scanner names them, and the other unfinished uploads (409 `name_taken` with `by`: `model`, `preset`, `alias`, `file`, `upload`; `other`, the name it collides with; `case_variant`); checked again at update and right before publishing.
- `files`: 1 to 256, each at least 24 bytes; `name` is only shown and used for matching after a reload, never as a path; an optional `sha256` (64 hex characters) is compared after the last byte (a mismatch makes the upload wait as `ready` / `sha256_mismatch`).
- `settings`: per-model settings (as `POST /admin/models/settings`, including the lock rules: 409 `field_locked`; `locks` shows the locks for this id, worked out from `[*]` and the router command line), saved as the model's per-model settings right before its files become visible, so its first start uses them. `settings_mode` `replace` (default) drops saved settings of an earlier model with this id, `keep` uses them again with `settings` on top (`existing_settings` shows them). Either way the entry is saved again as `pending`, so the first start of the new files is a trial with the automatic revert.
- `auto_publish` (default true): publish as soon as the checks pass.
- `dry_run`: check only, nothing is created (200, `upload.id` null; not counted against the 4 unfinished uploads).

`warnings` never block (disk space is warn-only): `not_enough_space`, `larger_than_disk`, `shares_disk_with_state` (Linux), `state_not_writable` (with settings the publish stops at `settings_not_saved`), `record_not_persisted`, and the value warnings of `POST /admin/models/settings`. The files are then sent with `POST /admin/models/upload/chunk`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Append one chunk of a file of an upload (exempt)
post.description:
The body is the raw bytes `offset .. offset + length - 1` of file `file` (at most `chunk_max`, 16 MiB; `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`). The server handles a chunk only once it has the whole body, so its offset moves by whole chunks only and sending a chunk again is always safe:

- `offset` equal to the server's offset: appended.
- `offset` before it: the part the server already has is compared byte for byte with what it stored (409 `content_mismatch` with the `offset` of the block that differs: not the same file); the rest, if any, is appended. A chunk wholly inside the stored bytes is answered 200 and writes nothing.
- `offset` after it: 409 `offset_mismatch` with the server's `offset`.

`verify=1` only compares and never writes (answer `verified`, `verified_bytes`): the way to check that a file picked again (after a reload, or by a script that continues an upload) is the one the server has, usually the first MiB (when `head_crc32` is null or not used) and the MiB before the server's offset. A body beyond the server's offset is not compared and not stored; a probe does not make its sender the one that writes.

`X-Upload-Client` names the sender (a random id per browser tab, kept for the tab session); a chunk from another sender within 30 s of the last one is 409 `other_client_active` unless `takeover=1` (a probe is refused the same way). `X-Chunk-CRC32` (optional) is checked before the bytes are stored (400 `crc_mismatch`). The first chunk of a file shows whether it is GGUF (422 `not_gguf`; what was stored of that file is discarded). Once its metadata has arrived the header check runs in the background: a file it finds unusable is marked (`file_error`), and its chunks then get 422 `file_rejected` (`file`, `reason`: the code, e.g. `adapter`; only that file: drop it with `update` or cancel); a model it cannot accept rejects the upload within seconds (unsupported architecture, inconsistent split set).

Answered before the body is read, in this order: an address the allow-list refuses (403), no or a wrong key (401; 503 without a key), a missing `Content-Length` or any `Transfer-Encoding`, also `chunked` next to a `Content-Length` (411), a `Content-Encoding` other than `identity` (415), a `Content-Length` above `chunk_max` (413 `chunk_too_large`, JSON; a 413 without this JSON comes from a proxy: send smaller chunks), a malformed `id` (400), an upload that is over (410) or busy (409 `upload_busy`), another sender (409 `other_client_active`), a chunk of this upload already on its way (409 `chunk_in_progress`), too many chunks at once (429 `upload_slots_busy`). Every answer of 400 or above closes the connection; a client that is still sending may see a reset connection, or behind a proxy a 502 that is not the server's JSON, and then asks `GET /admin/models/upload?id=` where to continue. Also expect upstream's 503 while the server starts and 401 from `--api-key`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Change an upload: name, settings, expected SHA-256, drop files (exempt)
post.description: Only while the upload is `receiving` or `ready`. A new `name` is checked as at create (409 `name_taken`); nothing is uploaded again, which is how an upload waiting as `ready` / `name_taken` is renamed. `settings` replaces the settings of the upload; `settings_mode` and `auto_publish` as at create. `files` sets (or with an empty string removes) the expected SHA-256 of files by `index`; `drop_files` takes files out of the upload (for example one that is not GGUF) and deletes their data at once; when the files that are left are all complete the checks start. An upload that waits as `ready` stays there: send `publish` next. Refused: dropping every file (400, cancel instead); dropping a file once the checks have arranged the files under their final names (409 `upload_busy` with `staged: true`: cancel and upload again without that file); 409 `upload_busy` while it is being checked or published, 410 once it is over. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

sha.summary: Correct the expected SHA-256 of file 0

409.description: `name_taken` (`by`, `other`, `case_variant`), `field_locked` (`param`), `upload_busy` (`state`; `staged: true` for a drop after the files were arranged for publishing)

post.summary: Publish an upload that waits as ready, or run its checks again (exempt)
post.description: For an upload in `ready`: `manual` (auto_publish off, or rebuilt without its record), after a rename (`name_taken`), after a `publish_error` or a `settings_invalid`. For `check_failed` and `sha256_mismatch` the checks run again (Retry; the SHA-256 is not computed again); `ignore_sha256_mismatch: true` accepts a SHA-256 that differs from the expected one (publish anyway). `without_settings: true` publishes without the upload's settings (`settings_not_saved`, `settings_invalid`; the model then starts with its inherited values). Publishing also switches `auto_publish` on. Publishing: the name is checked again, the settings are checked again and saved as the model's per-model settings (phase `pending`), the files become visible with one rename that never replaces anything (a failed rename puts the previous settings entry back), and the model list is rebuilt; the model then appears not loaded. Answers 202 at once (`publishing` or `checking`): follow it with `GET /admin/models/upload?id=`. An upload that is already published answers 200; one that is publishing or checking answers 202 with its state; 409 `upload_busy` while it is still receiving, 410 for a rejected, cancelled or expired one. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

anyway.summary: Publish anyway with a differing SHA-256

post.summary: Cancel an upload and delete its data (exempt)
post.description: Ends an upload that is not published yet and deletes its data at once (`cancelled`, `freed_bytes`). An upload that is being checked stops after the current step; one that is being published is refused (409). An upload that is already over answers 200 with `freed_bytes` 0 (`cancelled` is true only when it had been cancelled). **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Delete a model of the models directory, or only its projector (exempt)
post.description:
For models with source `models_dir` (uploaded or dropped in by hand); downloaded models keep `DELETE /models`, sections of `models.ini` are changed in `models.ini` (409 `not_deletable`). Only what the models directory gives this model is deleted: its GGUF file or every shard of a split model, and for a model in a folder the projector and draft model in that folder. Other entries of its folder stay (`kept`), and so does a projector or draft model that every model gets (a draft on the router command line, a projector or draft in the `[*]` section of `models.ini`: `kept` with `shared: true`); the folder is removed only when it is empty afterwards. `projector_only` (Remove projector) deletes only the model's own projector file; the model stays with its settings and pin.

- `dry_run`: only report (`files`, `n_files`, `total_bytes`; `kept`, at most 100 listed, `n_kept` (all entries that stay), `kept_truncated`, `kept_bytes`; `folder`, `folder_removed`; `running`, `status`, `pinned`, `has_settings`, `warnings`).
- A running model is refused (409 `model_running`) unless `stop`; then it is stopped first with a deadline of its stop timeout + 10 s (504 `stop_timeout`, nothing deleted).
- `remove_settings` (default true; ignored with `projector_only`) also removes the model's saved per-model settings, its pin and what the server cached about it.

The files are moved into a trash folder inside the models directory first (out of the model list at once), the model list is rebuilt, and the trash is deleted in the background (`trash_left`). An unknown id, or a model that is still being downloaded, is 409 `not_deletable` with `reason` `not_found` (never 404). **Exempt** from the trial budget.

get.description:
The activity log, newest record first, one page at a time. Kinds and their actions: `change`, an admin request with the key that changes something, with its outcome (`settings.update`, `model_settings.update`, `model_settings.reset`, `gpus.rescan`, `upload.create`, `upload.takeover`, `upload.cancel`, `upload.published`, `upload.rejected`, `model.delete`, `model.remove_projector`; result `error` with `status` and `code` (the error type) when the request failed and changed nothing; `upload.published` and `upload.rejected` are recorded when the checks end, with the actor of the admin who created the upload); `refusal`, `401` / `403` answers (`access.refused`, merged per client, path, status and reason for 60 s; the no-key status probe merged over all clients; at most 60 new records a minute and 256 open windows, the rest in one `access.refused_more` summary; kept in a file of their own so that they never push a change out of the log); `server`, actions of the server itself (`upload.expired`, `upload.resumed_after_restart`, `upload.swept` (recorded once the removal is done: `ok`, or `failed` once and then `ok` when a later sweep removed the folder), `model_settings.reverted`, `model_settings.reverted_at_startup`, `audit.started`, `audit.persisted_again`); `observed`, effects of the public model routes seen on the model status feed, actor "public API (unknown)" (`download.finished`, `download.failed`, `model.removed` (only from `DELETE /models`; files removed from the models directory by hand leave no record), `model.start_failed`; at most 30 a minute, the rest in one `observed.more`; a file of their own as well). Results: `ok`, `error`, `failed` (a GPU re-detection, a download or a model start did not work), `rejected`, `refused`. Read-only requests and single upload chunks are not recorded; who called the public routes (`/models`, `/models/load`, `/models/unload`) is not known. Never stored: `X-Admin-Key`, `Authorization`, `HF_TOKEN`, request bodies, paths outside the models directory.

A merged record is written at once with its first request and updated when its window ends; the page shows its latest version (`count`, `updated_seq`; `open` while it still counts) under the `seq` of its first line, so paging with `before` is stable.

Stored in `<admin state dir>/admin-audit.jsonl` (changes and server records), `admin-audit-refusals.jsonl` and `admin-audit-observed.jsonl`, each rotated to `.1` at 4 MiB (at most 24 MiB in all), lines of at most 4 KiB, each record synced to disk. When a file cannot be written its records go to a ring of the last 1000 in memory, one ring per file (`persisted: false`, warning `audit_not_persisted`); the file is tried again every minute, and once a write works the ring is written in order, then one `audit.persisted_again` into that file (recorded only once it is on disk; also for a file whose ring was empty). The admin action itself never fails or waits because of the log.

`format=jsonl` answers the lines themselves as a file (`application/x-ndjson`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`): every line of the three files, their `.1` and the memory rings, sorted by `seq` (oldest first); a merged record that ended with its first line and, when it counted more than one request, its update (`group` = the `seq` of its first line); a window still counting at the place of its first line, with its current count (its update follows when it ends); the filters and `before` apply, `limit` does not. This route itself is not recorded. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

values.description: `enum`: the allowed values; `ngl`: the words allowed besides a number

auto.description: The number that means auto (`-1` for `parallel`)

pair.description: The key this one must be equal to (`cache-type-k` / `cache-type-v`)

build_devices.description: GPUs of this server; empty for a CPU-only build

unattached.description: Saved settings of models that are not in the list; kept until removed with `reset`

warnings.description: `default_device_not_present`, `model_devices_unknown_section:<name>` (a MODEL_DEVICES entry that names no models.ini section)

AdminUnattachedEntry.description: Saved settings of a model that is not in the list (also the answer of `GET /admin/models/settings?model=<id>` for such an id, then with `state`)

kind.description: `orphaned`: the model is gone (deleted, renamed); `hidden`: a cache entry the list does not show; `unreadable`: an entry of the file that could not be read (kept as it is, see `raw`)

raw.description: `unreadable` only: the entry as it is in the file

error.description: Why the file could not be read; empty when fine

read_only.description: true = the file is damaged or from a newer version; saving answers 409 `model_settings_read_only`

backup_loaded.description: The file could not be read and its `.bak` was used

problems.description: Entries or values that were skipped while reading

model.description: Model id, or the id of an entry in `unattached`

reset.description: Remove all custom settings of the model

restart.description: Running model: restart it with the new settings (without it the change is refused with 409). Stopped model: load it right away

changed.description: false = the effective values did not change; nothing was reloaded or restarted

restarted_also.description: Other models that were loaded before, went down when the model list was rebuilt, and were loaded again

not_restarted.description: Other models that went down and could not be loaded again

load_error.description: Saved, but the model could not be started now (e.g. `model limit reached`); it starts on its next request. Empty when fine

reload_error.description: Always empty in a 200 answer: a failed rebuild of the model list is a 500 (`error.reload_error`) and the previous settings are restored

AdminReloadError.description: The error answer of `POST /admin/models/settings` when the settings could not be applied

reload_error.description: Why the model list could not be rebuilt (missing when the settings file could not be written)

restarted.description: Only when the model was running and had been stopped for the restart: true = it runs again with its previous settings, false = see `restart_error`

restarted_also.description: Only when not empty: other models that were loaded before and were loaded again

not_restarted.description: Only when not empty: other models that were loaded before and could not be loaded again

ok.description: false = llama.cpp could not set the model up with these settings, see `error`

cached.description: The result of an earlier check: same model, effective arguments, GPU inventory and running state, at most 60 s old, and the live free memory of its GPUs moved by less than 256 MiB

checked_while_running.description: The dry run was made while the model was running: its fit saw the model's own memory as used (missing in an answer with `ok: false`)

verdict.description: The worst verdict of all devices (`no`, then `unknown`, then `tight`); `cpu_only`: the model uses no GPU (a CPU-only server, or `device` `none`), `devices` is empty and `host` has its memory

need.description: Bytes the model would need on this GPU

free.description: Free memory of the GPU now

own_usage.description: What the model uses there now, counted as available when it is running and would be restarted

settling.description: A model on this GPU is loading or stopping: verdict `unknown`

verdict.description: `fits`: need + margin <= available; `tight`: need <= available < need + margin; `no`: need > available; `unknown`: memory not known or settling

host.description: Host memory the model would need (model, context, compute)

args.description: The command line of the dry run (what the model process would get)

duration_ms.description: How long a new check took (not in a cached answer)

n_gpu_layers.description: The GPU layers llama.cpp's fit chose

fit.description: Result of llama.cpp's fit (`off`: the fit was switched off for this model)

line.description: The output line of llama.cpp the code comes from

AdminGpuInventory.description: The GPUs the inventory helper found (at start-up, or at the last `POST /admin/gpus/rescan`)

error.description: Why it failed (`timeout`, `failed`, `parse_error`, `unsupported`, `disabled`); the GPU names then come from the backends only

name.description: Device name as the backend registers it (CUDA0, ROCm0, Vulkan0, SYCL0, ...)

device_id.description: Device id as the backend reports it

pci_bus_id.description: PCI bus id, lower case `dddd:bb:dd.f`; null when the backend reports none

mapping.description: How the vendor tool's row was matched to this GPU

index.description: Index of the vendor tool's row (not the device number)

unsupported.description: The tool reports no usable memory for this GPU (e.g. MIG, vGPU)

memory_source.description: `inventory` = measured at start-up / last re-detect, see `memory_age_ms`

settling.description: A model on this GPU is loading or stopping (or did so a moment ago): the free memory is not final

same_gpu_as.description: Other device names of the same physical GPU (e.g. CUDA0 and Vulkan0)

all_gpus.description: The model has no GPU of its own and may use every GPU

source.description: `reported` by the model process itself (its memory breakdown, printed at log verbosity 4), `measured` per process by nvidia-smi (host only), or a rough `estimate`

by.description: `model` (reported), `nvidia-smi` (measured), `llama.cpp` (estimate from a fit check of the current settings) or `formula` (estimate from the model file)

gpu_backend.description: The GPU backends of this server

state.description: `cpu_only`: no GPU backend in this build; `no_devices`: a GPU backend is there but found no GPU (driver, permissions such as /dev/kfd or /dev/dri, container without GPUs)

libraries.description: GPU backend libraries next to the binary

message.description: The error in words, e.g. the tool's first error line

stale.description: The last run failed; the figures are from an older run

mapping.description: How the tool's rows were matched to the GPUs: by PCI bus id, the one GPU with the one row, not at all, a mix, or no GPU

margin.description: Safety margin of the fit verdict (1 GiB, as llama.cpp's own fit)

unmatched.description: Rows of the vendor tool without a GPU of the server (e.g. hidden by CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES)

started_ms.description: `started` in milliseconds since the epoch: comparable with `last_failure.time_ms`, a greater value is a later start than the failure

id.description: `deployment`, `binary`, `gpu_backend`, `inventory`, `vendor_tool`, `memory_mapping`, `router_gpu_free`, `state_dir`, `models_storage` (the model cache and `--models-dir`: `warning` when one of them is not kept, the hint names the directories and what to mount), `admin_key`, `proxy`, `ip_allowlist`, `model_devices`, `model_settings`, `audit` (the value of `AdminAuditState` plus `files`; `warning` while the activity log is kept in memory), and `stuck_helpers` at the end, only while a helper process hangs

value.description: What was found: a string, a number, a boolean, an object or null

hint.description: One line on what to do or what it means

AdminUploadAvailability.description: Whether GGUF files can be uploaded on this server

reason.description: null when available. `no_models_dir`: no `--models-dir` (Docker: the entrypoint could not create `/models-rw/local`, a read-only mount? see the container log; host: add it to `PROVISION_LLM_ARGS`; then restart). `models_dir_missing`, `not_writable`: fix the directory. `staging_unusable`: `.provision-upload` in the models directory is a file or a symbolic link. `staging_other_filesystem`: something is mounted over `.provision-upload`

message.description: The reason in words, with what to do

chunk_default.description: Chunk size a client starts with

chunk_min.description: Smallest chunk a client steps down to when a proxy limits the request size

max_sessions.description: Unfinished uploads at the same time

max_writers.description: Chunks received at the same time over all uploads

ttl_h.description: Hours without progress after which an upload is removed (counted while the server runs)

max_header_bytes.description: Largest metadata section of a file

AdminUploadSummary.description: One upload in the list of `GET /admin/models/upload`

name.description: The model id it will get

substate.description: `checking`: `queued` (waiting for its turn: one upload is checked at a time), `hashing` (with `progress`; only when the SHA-256 is read again from disk), `classifying`, `load_check`

blocked_by.description: `ready` only: what the upload waits for; details in `blocked`

error.description: `rejected`: `code`, `message`, `file` (the index of the file the verdict is about, or null); `expired`: `code` `expired`

blocked.description: `ready`: `code` and `message`, and per `blocked_by`: `name_taken` `by`, `other`, `case_variant`; `sha256_mismatch` `file`, `expected`, `actual`; `check_failed` the code of why the check could not run (`timeout`, `spawn_failed`, `no_result`, `check_error`, `hash_failed`, `check_failed`, `staging_failed`; on Windows `path_too_long` with `max_name_length`; after a restart a file code such as `not_gguf` with `file`); `publish_error` `staging_failed`, `upload_unavailable`, `staging_other_filesystem`, `publish_failed` (`errno`); `settings_invalid` the settings error and `param`

expires_at.description: When it is removed without progress; set only while it is `receiving` or `ready`

staging_bytes.description: What the unfinished uploads take on disk

settings_writable.description: The placement of an upload can be saved (the admin state directory is writable); otherwise an upload with settings stops as `ready` / `settings_not_saved`

index.description: Position in `files` of the create request; the `file` of the chunk route

name.description: The original file name (shown and used for matching only, never a path)

offset.description: Bytes the server accepted; the next chunk starts here

durable_offset.description: Bytes known to be on disk (last checkpoint, every 256 MiB or 15 s); after a restart of the server `offset` goes back to it

dropped.description: Taken out of the upload with `drop_files`

role.description: From the file's header (a file with the architecture `clip` is the projector; `adapter` or `imatrix` for such a file, which is refused); null before

sha256.description: Computed while the file is received, so known once it is complete (after a restart of the server read again from disk)

head_crc32.description: CRC-32 of the first MiB (8 hex digits), once that much has arrived: compare it with a file picked again before continuing; null when the server does not know it (probe with `verify=1`)

final_name.description: The name in the models directory, once the classification has decided it

header.description: The header check of this file: `state` (`none`: no bytes yet, `scanning`: waiting for the rest of the metadata, `queued`, `ok`, `warning`: decided by the load check at the end, `failed`: the check could not run and runs again, `error`: refused, see `error`); once the metadata was read `arch` and `type` (`general.architecture` and `general.type` of the file, null when absent: `model`, `adapter`, `imatrix`, `mmproj`, or older values such as `clip-vision`) and `split` (`no`, `count`) for a shard; `message` only with a warning, a failure or a refusal

error.description: Why this file cannot be used (`code`, `message`): `not_gguf`, `adapter`, `imatrix`, `projector_bad_metadata`, `projector_without_modality`, `malformed`, `header_too_large`

settings.description: Per-model settings for the first start

plan.description: The final layout, once the classification has decided it: `layout` (`file` or `folder`), `target` (the name in the models directory), `id`, `files[]` (`index`, `final_name`, `role`, `split_no`: null for a single file)

facts.description: What the checks read about the model: `arch`, `name` (`general.name`), `n_params`, `n_ctx_train`, `n_layer`, `file_type` (`general.file_type`), `n_tensors`, `split` for a split set; after the load check also `n_vocab`, `desc`, and with a projector `vision` / `audio`

result.description: `published`: `model`, `layout`, `target`, `rename` (how the files were moved into place), `reload_error` (the model list could not be rebuilt; the next rescan lists the model), `settings_saved`, `files[]` (`name` relative to the models directory, `role`, `size`, `sha256`). An upload whose publish had finished when the server stopped shows only `model`, `target` and `recovered`

idle_ms.description: Time without progress, counted while the server runs

last_client_idle_ms.description: Time since the last chunk from any sender; below 30000 another sender gets `other_client_active`

recovered.description: The server took the upload over after a restart

recovered_without_record.description: Rebuilt from its staging hint alone (its record in the admin state directory was missing): without its settings, and it waits as `ready` / `manual` after its checks

record_persisted.description: The upload's record is in the admin state directory

checks.description: One entry per file whose header check has started: `step` (`header`), `file`, `status` (the `header.state` of that file), `message` (empty while all is well, otherwise the warning or the reason)

last_modified.description: Milliseconds since the epoch; a hint for matching the file after a reload

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 (as Hugging Face shows it)

settings_mode.description: Saved settings of an earlier model with this id: `replace` drops them, `keep` uses them again with `settings` on top

upload.description: The new upload, as `GET /admin/models/upload?id=` shows it; in a dry run only `id` (null), `name`, `files` (`index`, `name`, `size`), `settings` (as they would be saved), `chunk_max`, `chunk_default`

disk.description: The filesystem of the models directory

other_uploads_bytes.description: What the other unfinished uploads still need

shares_disk_with.description: Other data on the same filesystem: `admin_state` (checked on Linux only)

warnings.description: Never blocking: `not_enough_space` (larger than the free space minus what other unfinished uploads still need), `larger_than_disk`, `shares_disk_with_state` (a full disk would also stop settings from being saved), `state_not_writable` (the admin state directory cannot be written: with settings the publish stops at `settings_not_saved`), `record_not_persisted` (the record could not be written to the admin state directory), and the value warnings of `POST /admin/models/settings` (e.g. `ctx_above_train`, `device_missing`)

locks.description: The settings that are locked for this model: `{ key: { by, value } }`, `by` `router_cli` (given on the router command line) or `model_devices` (the GPU of a `MODEL_DEVICES` `*=` entry in `[*]`)

existing_settings.description: Only when there are some: saved settings of an earlier model with this id (an `orphaned` entry of `GET /admin/models/settings`)

offset.description: The file's offset on the server after this chunk

state.description: The upload's state; `checking` once every file is complete

file_error.description: Why this file cannot be used, once the header check decided so

AdminUploadVerifyResult.description: Answer of a chunk sent with `verify=1`: compared, nothing written

verified.description: Always true in a 200 answer (a difference is 409 `content_mismatch`)

verified_bytes.description: How much of the body overlapped the stored bytes and was compared

offset.description: The file's offset on the server

files.description: Set the expected SHA-256 of files (an empty string removes it)

drop_files.description: Indexes of files to take out of the upload; their data is deleted at once. Refused (409 `upload_busy`, `staged: true`) once the checks have arranged the files under their final names

ignore_sha256_mismatch.description: Publish although the SHA-256 differs from the expected one

without_settings.description: Publish without the upload's settings (when they cannot be saved, `settings_not_saved`, or no longer fit, `settings_invalid`)

AdminUploadAnswer.description: Answer of update, publish and cancel

dry_run.description: Only report what would be deleted

stop.description: Stop the model first if it is running (otherwise 409 `model_running`)

remove_settings.description: Also remove its saved per-model settings, its pin and what the server cached about it

projector_only.description: Remove projector: delete only the model's projector file

files.description: What is (would be) deleted, paths relative to the models directory

kept.description: What stays: the other entries of the model's folder (not part of this model; `bytes` null for a folder) and, with `shared: true`, a projector or draft model that every model gets; at most 100 listed

shared.description: A projector or draft model every model gets (a draft on the router command line, `[*]` of `models.ini`): never deleted from here

dry_run.description: True in the answer of a dry run

n_kept.description: The number of all entries that stay; larger than the length of `kept` when that list is cut at 100

kept_truncated.description: Dry run: `kept` lists only the first 100 of `n_kept` entries

kept_bytes.description: The size of all files that stay

folder.description: The model's folder in the models directory; null for a top-level file

folder_removed.description: The folder is (would be) empty afterwards and removed

running.description: Dry run: the model is running (it would be stopped with `stop`)

has_settings.description: Dry run: the model has saved per-model settings

warnings.description: Dry run: `running`, `folder_keeps_other_model` (another GGUF file stays in the folder and may be listed under this id afterwards)

trash_left.description: The files wait in the trash, which the server deletes in the background

reload_error.description: The model list could not be rebuilt afterwards; the files are gone all the same

AdminAuditState.description: Whether the activity log is written to the admin state directory (`audit` of `GET /admin/status` and `GET /admin/audit`)

persisted.description: false while records of any of the three files (changes, refusals, observed) are kept in memory

error.example: the admin state directory cannot be written
error.description: Why not; null when it is written

since.description: Since when records are kept in memory

in_memory.description: Records waiting in memory to be written (all files)

lost.description: Records the full memory rings dropped meanwhile

max_bytes.description: A file is rotated to `.1` when it would grow past this

ring_max.description: Records the memory ring holds (per file)

AdminAuditActor.description: Who caused a record. There are no user accounts: an admin request is identified by its address and `User-Agent`; whoever presents the admin key is the same admin. Header values are printable ASCII (other bytes become `?`) and cut

type.description: `client`: an admin request (the fields below); `server`: the server itself; `public_api`: an effect of the public model routes; `various`: a merged record of several clients (the status probe of refused browsers, the summary of a flood)

label.description: The actor in one line: `10.64.0.7`, `10.64.0.7 via trusted proxy 127.0.0.1`, `172.18.0.3 (X-Forwarded-For 10.64.0.7, unverified)`, `server`, `public API (unknown)`, `browsers of refused addresses`, `several clients`

peer.description: The TCP peer of the request; behind nginx or another proxy, the proxy (`unix socket` for a Unix socket)

client.description: The client address as the address logic of `PROVISION_ADMIN_ALLOW_FROM` finds it, also while that allow-list is off: the peer, or, only when the peer is listed in `PROVISION_ADMIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, the address taken from its `X-Forwarded-For`; empty when unknown

via_proxy.description: `client` was taken from the `X-Forwarded-For` of a trusted proxy

forwarded_for.description: Only when the request had one: the raw `X-Forwarded-For` (several header lines joined with `, `, in the order they arrived), at most 128 bytes

forwarded_trusted.description: With `forwarded_for`: the peer is a trusted proxy. false: the header is whatever the sender wrote (unverified)

note.example: X-Forwarded-For was sent more than once
note.description: Why the `X-Forwarded-For` of a trusted proxy was not used: missing, sent in more than one header line (in any spelling of its name), or an entry that is not an address

user_agent.description: Only when the request had one: the `User-Agent` header, at most 128 bytes; written by the client, proves nothing

AdminAuditEntry.description: One record of the activity log: the fields of its line in the file (at most 4 KiB) plus `id`, `persisted`, `open` and `updated_seq`. A line whose start can be read but not the rest (`unreadable`) has only `seq`, `kind`, `action`, `result`

seq.description: Numbers the records of the three files in the order they were recorded, across restarts; for a merged record the `seq` of its first line. `before` of `GET /admin/audit` refers to it

kind.description: `change`: an admin request that changes something; `refusal`: a refused admin request; `server`: an action of the server itself; `observed`: an effect of the public model routes

result.description: `ok`; `error`: the admin request was answered with an error and changed nothing (`details`: `status`, `code`); `failed`: the action did not work (GPU re-detection, download, model start); `rejected`: the checks refused an upload; `refused`: a `401` / `403`

ts.description: When it was recorded, in milliseconds since 1970; for a merged record its first request

target.description: The model id, upload name or path the action is about (printable ASCII, at most 256 bytes); empty when there is none

details.description: Per action (docs/provision-admin.md, section 18.1): `changes` as `{key: {from, to}}` (each value at most 128 bytes of JSON), `changed`, upload `id`, `bytes`, `files`, `layout`, `sha256`, `arch`, reason `code`, deleted `paths` (relative to the models directory). A merged record: `count`, `first`, `last`, for a refusal `status`, `code`, `reason`, `probe`; with several clients `clients`, `clients_capped`, `sample` (at most 8 addresses); a summary also `items`, `items_capped` (at most 16 paths or model ids). Details that did not fit in the 4 KiB line: `truncated: true` and `text` (the first KiB of their JSON text). Never a key, a token, a request body or a path outside the models directory

count.description: A merged record: the requests or events it stands for

truncated.description: The record did not fit in 4 KiB even with its details cut: only `seq`, `kind`, `action`, `result`, `ts` and `time` are kept

persisted.description: false for a record that is only in memory

open.description: A merged record whose 60 s are not over: its `count` still grows

updated_seq.description: A merged record: the `seq` of its latest update; a window still counting (`open`) has no update yet: its own `seq`

unreadable.description: The line could not be read back (written by hand or cut by a crash; the next record still starts on a line of its own); only the head fields are given

next_before.description: Send it as `before` for the next older page; null when there is nothing older (with the filters applied)

matched.description: How many records match the filters and `before` in all, this page included

persisted.description: false while any of the three files of the log is kept in memory

param.description: Admin validation and lock errors: the request field the error is about, a key of `settings` (e.g. `ctx-size`), `settings` or `model`

license.description: Present on 403 responses from the license gate

max_tokens.description: OpenAI name; native alias is n_predict

input.description: A string, or a list of input items
A string or array of strings to embed

query.example: What is the capital of France?

documents.description: Candidate documents to score against the query

top_n.description: Return only the top N results

index.description: Index into the input documents array

prompt.description: Optional extra prompt inserted between prefix and suffix
